greetings: Ah, a traveler! Come into the shade before the sun fries your brain like an egg on a stone.
Greetings! The bazaar is bustling, but my tent is an oasis of wisdom.
The sands shift, but my prices remain rock solid. Which means very high.
guild_master.reward: Take this enchanted lamp. No djinns inside, I checked. Mostly just lint.

generic: I've got sand in my sandals, sand in my robes, and I think I swallowed a dune.
Do you hear the singing sands? Or is that just the cleric humming off-key again?
May your water skin never run dry, and your camel never spit in your face.
If you find a lamp, rub it. If a djinn comes out, tell him he owes me five emeralds.
The oasis is beautiful today. A perfect place to pretend I'm not avoiding work.
I swear by the beard of my ancestors, I saw a cactus move. This desert is haunted.
It is said the desert tests a man's soul. So far, my soul is just very thirsty.
Watch out for the husks. They have zero respect for personal space.
My mother was a dune, my father was a sandstorm. Just kidding, they were bakers.
I tried to build a sandcastle once. The wind laughed at me.

farmer: Growing wheat in the desert? It's not a profession, it's an extreme sport.
I asked the sky for rain, and a bird pooped on me. The gods have a twisted sense of humor.
My melons are the juiciest in the bazaar! Just ignore the sand crunch.
The secret to desert farming? Cry over the crops. They need the moisture.
I am the master of the oasis! Bow before my... slightly wilted carrots.
A merchant offered me magic beans. I traded him a handful of hot sand.
To tame the harsh sands requires patience, discipline, and a very large watering can.
I chased a rabbit away from my crops. It stopped, judged my irrigation technique, and left.
Some say the desert is barren. I say they just don't know how to talk to the dirt.
Life is like a cactus. Prickly, green, and occasionally sprouts a weird flower.
fisherman: Yes, I fish in the desert. No, I haven't caught anything since Tuesday.
The oasis is small, but the fish are cunning. They know my face.
I cast my line into the dunes. Sometimes I catch a scorpion. Good eating.
A true fisherman does not need a river. He only needs delusion and a nice hat.
I once hooked a djinn's lamp. He was very annoyed about the bait.
The water reflects the endless sky, and my endless failure to catch a salmon.
I'm actually just washing my string. Don't tell the others.
Sand trout! They exist! You just have to dig really, really fast.
I stare into the water waiting for a bite. The water stares back, judging me.
Patience is the anchor of the soul. Also, I fell asleep.
shepherd: My sheep are 50% wool, 50% sand, and 100% annoying.
I sheared a sheep yesterday. Under the wool, it was just three cacti in a trench coat.
Guiding the flock through the dunes is a noble task. Mostly they just eat sand.
The desert wind howls, but my sheep just go 'baa'. It's very anti-climactic.
I knit a sweater out of camel hair once. It was so itchy I almost exiled myself.
A wolf tried to take one of my sheep. The sheep spat at him. We are built different here.
The bond between a shepherd and his flock is sacred. Also, they owe me money.
I painted my sheep yellow so they blend in with the sand. Now I can't find them.
Be still, and listen to the wisdom of the herd. They are saying... 'more grass'.
I am a master of the shears. I once gave a cactus a fade.
fletcher: Arrows fly straighter when the wind isn't blowing sand in your eyes. Sadly, it always is.
I fletch my arrows with the feathers of desert eagles. Or pigeons, don't tell the guards.
A bow is like a hawk: elegant, deadly, and really annoying to string.
I tried making an arrow out of a cactus spine. It was a very bad idea.
Precision is everything. I once shot a fly off a camel's nose. The camel was not amused.
Buy my arrows! They are guaranteed to hit something. Eventually.
The trajectory of a projectile is a beautiful mathematical truth. Also, swoosh!
I traded ten arrows for a block of sand. I am not a very good businessman.
A quiver full of arrows is a quiver full of hope. And splinters.
Don't shoot arrows into the sun. It won't shoot back, but it will blind you.
cleric: I read the ancient scrolls. Mostly they're just recipes for hummus.
The spirits of the sands speak to me! They say... 'drink more water'.
I brewed a potion of healing, but it tastes like old camel socks.
The glowstone illuminates the path of righteousness. It also attracts a lot of moths.
I sought enlightenment in the deep desert. I found a very angry scorpion.
To understand the divine, one must understand the lapis lazuli. It's blue. Very blue.
I offer blessings for a small fee. Emeralds preferred, goats accepted.
The brewing stand bubbles with the secrets of the universe. And also my lunch.
Do not fear the darkness, for the light shall guide you. Unless you forgot a torch.
I am the conduit of the mystical! Please wipe your sandals before entering.
weaponsmith: A scimitar curved like the crescent moon! Perfect for slicing melons. And heads.
I forged this blade in the heat of the midday sun. And a furnace. Mostly the furnace.
The iron speaks to me as I hammer it. It usually says 'ow'.
A warrior needs a good blade. Or a really heavy rock. I sell the blades.
I polished a sword so well I blinded myself for three days.
The clash of steel is the music of the desert. Well, that and the wind.
I tried to forge a sword out of sandstone. It broke immediately. I am a visionary, not a genius.
An unsharpened sword is just a very expensive stick.
I sell weapons of honor! And also pointy things for poking people you don't like.
The forge is hot, but the desert is hotter. I really need a vacation.
armorer: Chainmail in the desert? Excellent way to slow-cook yourself.
I crafted a helmet that perfectly deflects the sun. Unfortunately, you can't see out of it.
Armor protects the body, but only wisdom protects the soul. Still, buy the armor.
I make chestplates that can stop an arrow and hide your belly.
The clang of the anvil is my heartbeat. I probably should see a cleric about that.
I tried to make armor out of cactus. It was a defensive triumph and an ergonomic disaster.
A true warrior wears his scars with pride. But wearing my armor is much less painful.
Iron is strong, but a good bluff is lighter to carry.
I can custom-fit a helmet to the exact shape of your weird, lumpy head.
Sweat, soot, and steel. The glamour of the armorer's life.
toolsmith: A golden pickaxe! It will break in five minutes, but you'll look fabulous doing it.
I make shovels that can dig through the densest dunes. Or just lean against a wall nicely.
The right tool for the right job. Unless the job is fighting a creeper, then just run.
I forged a hoe so sharp it cuts through time itself. Or just dirt.
A well-made axe is a lumberjack's best friend. Assuming you can find a tree.
I sell pickaxes! Because punching stone is a really bad life choice.
The durability of diamond, the elegance of iron, the price of... a lot of emeralds.
I accidentally glued my hand to a shovel once. It was a very productive day.
Every tool has a purpose. Even the wooden hoe. Its purpose is to be mocked.
Craftsmanship is an art. And I am the Michelangelo of pointy sticks.
butcher: Fresh meat! Guaranteed not to be camel. Probably.
The desert sun dries the jerky perfectly. Just don't ask about the flies.
I have a degree in meat sciences. It's a very specialized field.
A sharp cleaver and a steady hand. That's how you deal with difficult customers.
I made a sausage so spicy it burned a hole in my cutting board.
Raw mutton? Only if you want to meet the cleric very soon.
The circle of life is beautiful. And delicious with a little garlic.
I once tried to butcher a cactus. I lost.
Come, taste the finest cuts of the oasis! Ignore the sand, it adds texture.
A good butcher respects the animal. And then charges a premium for the chops.
leatherworker: Leather pants in the desert? You are either very brave or very foolish.
I tan my hides under the blazing sun. It smells terrible, but the results are... okay.
A good leather tunic breathes well. Unlike the person wearing it in a sandstorm.
I made a saddle so comfortable, the horse fell asleep.
Dyeing leather is an art. Today's color is 'desert dust brown'. Same as yesterday.
I tried to make a leather water skin, but I accidentally made a bagpipe.
The durability of cowhide, the flexibility of... well, cowhide.
I sell the finest leather caps! Perfect for hiding your bald spot.
A true artisan knows the grain of the leather. A bad artisan just glues it together.
If you buy my pants, I'll throw in a free lesson on how to walk without squeaking.
mason: Sandstone, sandstone, and more sandstone. I dream in shades of beige.
I carved a magnificent statue of a djinn. Then it crumbled. Typical.
The foundation of society is a well-cut block. And maybe some good laws.
I can cut stone so precisely, you can't even fit a grain of sand between the blocks.
Chiseled sandstone is just regular sandstone with a superiority complex.
I accidentally built a wall around myself once. Took me three days to mine out.
A house of dirt is an insult to the earth. A house of stone is an insult to my back.
I appreciate the geometry of the pyramids, but their interior design is very lacking.
Stone endures. Unlike my patience when you try to haggle.
The mortar must be mixed with the right ratio of water and sand. And sweat.
cartographer: I map the shifting dunes! It's a terrible job because the map is wrong by Tuesday.
Here is a map of the ocean. It's mostly blue. Very insightful, I know.
To explore the unknown is a grand adventure. To sell maps of it is a great business.
I drew a map to a hidden treasure! But I lost the map. And the treasure was just my lunch.
A compass points north. Unless you're near a magnet, then it points to trouble.
I charted the entire oasis. It's a circle. With water in the middle.
The world is vast and full of wonders. And also very large spiders.
I tried to map a mirage once. I got very wet and very confused.
A map is a window to the world. A window you have to pay me for.
Geography is destiny! Or at least, it tells you where not to build a house.
librarian: Silence in the library! Even if the library is just a tent and three books.
I have a book on the history of sand. It is very dry reading.
Knowledge is power. But a good enchanted book is Mending.
I trade wisdom for emeralds. It's a flawless business model.
I dropped a book in a puddle. It is now a tragic novel.
The words on the page contain the secrets of the ancients. And a really good falafel recipe.
I read a book on how to survive a creeper explosion. The last page was missing.
A well-organized bookshelf is a sign of a civilized mind. And too much free time.
I offer you the enchantment of Unbreaking! Please don't ask how it works.
Do not dog-ear the pages! I will curse your bloodline with minor inconveniences.
nitwit: I looked at the sun today. It looked back. We have an understanding.
Everyone says I should get a job. But watching the sand blow is a full-time commitment.
I found a shiny rock. I licked it. It tasted like regret.
The meaning of life is... wait, I forgot. Was it melons?
I tried to have a conversation with a cactus. It made some good points.
If you walk backwards, do you go back in time? I'm testing this hypothesis.
I'm not lazy, I'm just conserving energy for a future emergency. Like a nap.
I hear the wind whispering my name. It says 'get out of the way, idiot'.
I collected a jar of desert air. It's my most prized possession.
Sometimes I pretend I'm a block of sand. Just... existing.
none: I am currently between professions. Which is a fancy way of saying I am unemployed.
I thought about being a farmer, but I'm allergic to effort.
The bazaar is full of opportunities! I am ignoring all of them.
I am waiting for a sign from the heavens to choose my path. A lightning strike would do.
Maybe I'll become an adventurer like you! ...Nah, I like my knees un-arrowed.
I am a blank canvas! A very bored, slightly sandy blank canvas.
I asked the guild master for advice. He told me to go stand in the sun.
I'm considering a career in professional sand-castle building. The market is wide open.
Unemployment is a state of mind. A very relaxing, penniless state of mind.
I'm just here for the free shade.
